checks.note: I opened the arXiv HTML. The 1,642 traces, all 14 per-mode percentages, the 41% to 86.7% failure-rate range, human kappa 0.88, and the o1 judge's kappa 0.77 and accuracy 0.94 all match. The seven systems and the model list match too, and one figure caption does name six systems. There are three corrections. First, the interventions were run on AG2 (GSM-Plus, with GPT-4 and GPT-4o) as well as ChatDev, so 'one system' is wrong. Second, the ChatDev gains are percentage points on ProgramDev-v0: from 25.0 to 34.4 with the improved prompt/role specification, which includes the CEO having the final say (+9.4), and to 40.6 with the new topology/verification (+15.6). Third, I could not confirm '30 human-annotated traces per system (210)'. The text I read mentions 21 traces in MAST-Data-human, each annotated by three experts, and an initial 150-trace analysis. The paper says the ChatDev changes are not substantial improvements. The category sums are the reader's own arithmetic.
checks.corrected_claim: The mode percentages are as stated. The interventions were run on ChatDev and on AG2. On ChatDev ProgramDev-v0, task success went from 25.0% to 34.4% with an improved prompt/role specification (CEO has final say) and to 40.6% with a new topology/verification step, and the authors call these gains not substantial. The number of human-annotated traces is not 210 as far as I could see: the paper mentions 21 traces in MAST-Data-human with three annotators each.
checks.corrected_number: ChatDev ProgramDev-v0: 25.0 -> 34.4 (+9.4 pp) and 25.0 -> 40.6 (+15.6 pp). AG2 GSM-Plus with GPT-4o: 84.25 -> 89.00 / 88.83.
checks.conditions_that_limit_it: 7 open-source MAS frameworks, mostly GPT-4o with a few other models, and benchmarks that are not comparable across systems. Most labels come from an o1 LLM judge (kappa 0.77 against humans). The authors built both the taxonomy and the labels. I found no independent replication. The interventions are small-sample: 32 ProgramDev tasks.

checks.note: I opened the arXiv HTML. The abstract gives 53.5% (agent level) and 14.2% (step level), and says o1/R1 are not practical for this. Table 1 matches: All-at-Once 54.33 and 55.17 agent level; Step-by-Step 25.51 step level; random 29.10/12.00 and 19.06/4.16; Step-by-Step without ground truth 26.02, below random. Accuracy falls toward about 0% at the longest logs (93-130 steps). There are two corrections. The dataset split is 126 algorithm-generated (98 GAIA + 28 AssistantBench) and 58 hand-crafted (30 + 28), which sums to 184; it is not 98/86. And step-level accuracy on hand-crafted systems ranges from 3.51 to 8.77 across methods, not 5 to 9.
checks.corrected_claim: The claim is as stated, with these corrections: the dataset is 126 algorithm-generated plus 58 hand-crafted failure logs (184 in total), and hand-crafted step-level accuracy is 3.5-8.8%. All-at-Once without ground truth (3.51) is below random (4.16).
checks.corrected_number: Agent level best 54.33/55.17. Step level best 25.51 (algorithm-generated) and 3.51-8.77 (hand-crafted). Dataset 126 + 58 = 184.
checks.conditions_that_limit_it: Who&When is one dataset built by the authors: CaptainAgent-generated systems and Magentic-One on GAIA/AssistantBench, with GPT-4o as the main judge model and o1/R1 tested in a small table. 184 failure logs. I found no independent replication.

checks.note: I opened the abstract and the HTML v3. Table 5 gives amplification of 17.2/7.8/5.1/4.4, and task level is about 1.1-1.3. Finance centralized is +80.8% (0.631 vs 0.349); PlanCraft independent -70.0% and centralized -50.3%; SWE-bench Verified centralized -3.1% and independent -14.9%; BrowseComp-Plus independent about -35% (from a figure caption). The mean is -0.3% (CI -58.7 to +77.2). The ceiling term is beta -0.236, p=0.004, at about 45%. The amplification main effect is beta 0.014, p=0.658. Cross-validated R-squared is 0.373. Models: GPT-5-nano/mini/5, Gemini 2.0 Flash/2.5 Flash/2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 3.7/4/4.5. Sonnet 3.7 is excluded from SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench.
checks.conditions_that_limit_it: Six benchmarks, 260 configurations, nine models from three vendors. This is a regression over configurations with modest fit (R-squared 0.373). The architectures are the authors' own implementations. Industry/academic authors; I found no independent replication. I read only part of the HTML.

checks.note: I opened the arXiv HTML. Table 4 gives linear -23.72, flat -10.54 and hierarchical -5.51, and the current abstract gives 23.7/10.5/5.5%. The Conclusion's 12.1% and 9.2% for hierarchical do not match. All the Self-collab and Camel numbers match, and 96.4% is Self-collab with AutoTransform under both defenses. Defaults: Pm=1.0 and Pe=0.2. GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o at temperature 0. I did not check the earlier version's abstract figures.
checks.conditions_that_limit_it: Errors are synthetic (injected by AutoTransform/AutoInject), in six systems, on four small tasks, with GPT-3.5/GPT-4o only. Most factor analysis is GPT-3.5. Recovery is much smaller on flat Camel (to 48.7 against a baseline of 62.2). I found no independent replication.

checks.note: I opened the abstract and the HTML. Survival is 60.7/58.4/16.2 and McNemar against End-Check is 122.24 (136.10 against no verification). Gate 1 detects 75.4%. Escape rates are 24.6/48.3/89.3%. GPT-4o detection is 72.0% falling to 50.9%, and Qwen3.5-397B is 87.0%. Quality falls 4.44 to 3.93. 54.0% of errors are corrected against 76.9% flagged. 346 errors over 140 questions. The main pipeline is gpt-4o-mini and the gate experiment is gemini-2.5-flash. The limitations are as stated. v1 was submitted 22 June 2026 and was accepted at an ICML 2026 workshop (FAGEN).
checks.conditions_that_limit_it: A single workshop paper. Finance only (FinanceBench). A linear four-agent pipeline. Errors are regex-injected numeric shifts of 15-40%. Detection is judged by gpt-4o. Structured handoffs were not tested. Not independently replicated.

checks.note: I read the abstract page only. 0.422 -> 0.272, factor 0.644, accuracy 0.789 -> 0.769, -0.072 per transition, 500 experiments, 10 domains, 1,250 responses. The models are GPT-5.3, DeepSeek-V3 and LLaMA-3-70B-Instruct. I did not open the related paper 2606.07941, so its 1.34 figure is unchecked.
checks.conditions_that_limit_it: A preprint, read from its abstract only. Three-agent chains of refinement on knowledge questions, with natural inconsistencies rather than injected ones. The scoring method is not seen. No other topologies and no replication.

checks.note: I opened the arXiv HTML. 30.1% against 80.7%. GPT-4.1: baseline 0.037, Reveal-All 0.926, Secretary 0.241, Exchange-then-Decide 0.800. Gemini-2.5-Flash Secretary 0.713. Share-all prompt 0.467. +0.348 at 3 agents against +0.006 at 7. 65 tasks, 15 models, 10 sessions, 96 humans, CMU authors. The group-size comparison uses few tasks (7 and 5).
checks.conditions_that_limit_it: Hidden-profile puzzle tasks. Ablations mainly on GPT-4.1 and Gemini-2.5-Flash over 18 tasks, and the group-size result rests on 5-7 tasks. Not research workflows. No independent replication.

checks.note: I opened the arXiv HTML. The survival numbers match: 0.954->0.690, 0.880->0.580, 0.915->0.557, with facts at 0.97-1.00. Leakage is 48/48 and 37/48 without a marker and 2/48 and 1/48 with one. The typed allowlist gives 0/48 for GPT-5-mini and DeepSeek but 4/48 for Qwen3-32B. A corrupted allowlist gives 44/38/35 of 48. Three-hop partial recall loses -0.381 for GPT-5-mini. 36 scenarios, 7 domains, 4 surfaces, 5 conditions, kappa 0.74. The abstract's 0.80 baseline does not match the tables. Correction: the 25/32/39% absent figures are per marker, not per summary.
checks.corrected_claim: The claim is as stated, with two corrections. 25%, 32% and 39% of markers, not of summaries, were scored fully absent. And the typed allowlist gave 0/48 leakage for two models but 4/48 for Qwen3-32B.
checks.corrected_number: Markers absent 25/32/39% (per marker). Allowlist leakage 0/48, 0/48 and 4/48 (Qwen3-32B).
checks.conditions_that_limit_it: 36 hand-written synthetic scenarios, English only, simulated audiences, an LLM judge (kappa 0.74), three models. A single preprint from one group, not replicated.

checks.note: I opened the Factory article. Overall 3.70/3.44/3.35. Artifact trail 2.45/2.33/2.19, the weakest dimension for all three. Accuracy 4.04/3.74/3.43. Instruction following 4.99/4.95/4.92. 98.6/98.7/99.3% of tokens removed. 36,611 messages, four probes, a blind GPT-5.2 judge. The article argues that re-fetching can cost more tokens than compression saves; this is stated, not measured.
checks.conditions_that_limit_it: A vendor evaluation of its own product against competitors. The probes and rubric are its own, the judge is an LLM, the session count is not given, and the sessions are coding agents. No third-party replication.

checks.note: I opened the arXiv HTML. The paper makes the telephone-game argument. Table 1: executability 3.75 vs 2.25, revision cost 0.83 vs 2.5 (2.25 without feedback), tokens 31,255 vs 19,292, productivity 124.3 vs 248.9. Productivity is tokens per line, so lower is better for MetaGPT. The role ablation goes from 1.0 to 4.0 executability and 10 to 2.5 revisions. HumanEval 85.9 and MBPP 87.7. Feedback adds 4.2 and 5.4 points. It is correct that the ablation does not isolate the effect of the format.
checks.conditions_that_limit_it: SoftwareDev is a small, author-built set of software tasks scored by the authors. The comparison is against ChatDev only, in a 2023 setup with GPT-4-era models. Documents and roles are confounded.

checks.note: I opened the Anthropic engineering post. It gives 90.2%, about 4x and about 15x tokens, 80% of variance from tokens alone and 95% with tool calls and model choice, up to 90% less time, about 20 queries, and a single-call 0.0-1.0 judge with a pass/fail grade. It recommends external storage and lightweight references to reduce the telephone-game loss. It gives no measured number for information saved.
checks.conditions_that_limit_it: An internal evaluation by the product team, with no public data, methods or sample size. The telephone-game point is design rationale, not measured. BrowseComp variance analysis only.

checks.note: I opened the arXiv HTML. GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 -> 91.5 -> 89.0. CommonSenseQA 82.0 -> 79.5 -> 80.0. HotpotQA 49.0 -> 49.0 -> 43.0 on 100 questions. GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 -> 38.1. With oracle labels, GSM8K reaches 97.5. Table 7: debate 83.2 (6 responses) and 83.0 (9), against self-consistency 85.3 and 88.2. The debate comparison appears to use GPT-3.5 (standard prompting 76.7), not GPT-4. I did not open the Kamoi survey.
checks.conditions_that_limit_it: GPT-3.5/GPT-4, plus GPT-4-Turbo and Llama-2, on three reasoning benchmarks with one prompt format. HotpotQA has only 100 questions. The debate comparison is on GSM8K with GPT-3.5. The finding is about intrinsic self-correction with no external feedback.

checks.note: I read the abstract page only. It supports the 63% preference, that the critic catches more bugs than paid contractors, that critics hallucinate bugs, that human-plus-critic teams catch about as many bugs while hallucinating less, and the hundreds of errors in 'flawless' data, mostly outside code. The abstract gives no catch-rate or hallucination-rate numbers.
checks.conditions_that_limit_it: An RLHF-trained OpenAI critic, not a prompted agent. Code review compared with paid contractors. Partly inserted bugs. Run by the developers. I read the abstract only.

checks.note: I opened the arXiv HTML for 2506.07962 and for Goel et al. (2502.04313). Agreement when both models are wrong is 0.423 (random about 0.127) and 0.6 (random 1/3), and 100% and 97.5% of pairs exceed chance. Same company +0.066/+0.022/+0.021 (resumes not significant, p=0.092). Same architecture +0.076 (leaderboard only). Higher accuracy predicts more correlation. Judge inflation is shown in figures, with no single number. In Goel et al., the average Pearson r is 0.84, and partial correlations controlling for accuracy are 0.35-0.65 (Section 3.2, Table 2). The RAG study was not opened.
checks.conditions_that_limit_it: Multiple-choice benchmark data (349/71 models) and a resume-matching set of 20 models. This measures overlapping blind spots in general, not a checker inside a workflow. An academic group. Goel et al. is a related, independent study with a similar finding.
